questions.stem:
Regarding the hydrides of group 15 elements $\mathrm{EH_3}$ (E = N, P, As, Sb), select the correct statement from the following:
A. The stability of hydrides decreases down the group.
B. The basicity of hydrides decreases down the group.
C. The reducing character increases down the group.
D. The boiling point increases down the group.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Stability order : $\mathrm{NH_3 > PH_3 > AsH_3 > SbH_3}$
Lewis Basic Strength : $\mathrm{NH_3 > PH_3 > AsH_3 > SbH_3}$
Reducing character : $\mathrm{NH_3 < PH_3 < AsH_3 < SbH_3}$
Boiling point : $\mathrm{PH_3 < AsH_3 < NH_3 < SbH_3}$

questions.stem:
An organic compound undergoes first order decomposition. The time taken for decomposition to $\left(\frac{1}{8}\right)^{th}$ and $\left(\frac{1}{10}\right)^{th}$ of its initial concentration are $t_{1/8}$ and $t_{1/10}$ respectively.
What is the value of $\frac{t_{1/8}}{t_{1/10}} \times 10$ ? ($\log 2 = 0.3$)
questions.solution:
$1^{st}$ order rate constant (k) = $\frac{2.303}{t}\log\left(\frac{C_0}{C_t}\right)$
$t_{1/8} = \frac{2.303}{k}\log\left(\frac{C_o}{\frac{C_o}{8}}\right)$
$t_{1/10} = \frac{2.303}{k}\log\left(\frac{C}{\frac{C_o}{10}}\right)$
$\frac{t_{1/8}}{t_{1/10}} = \frac{\log 8}{\log 10} = 0.9$
$\frac{t_{1/8}}{t_{1/10}} \times 10 = 9$

questions.stem: At T(K), 2 moles of liquid A and 3 moles of liquid B are mixed. The vapour pressure of ideal solution formed is 320 mm Hg . At this stage, one mole of A and one mole of B are added to the solution. The vapour pressure is now measured as 328.6 mm Hg . The vapour pressure (in mm Hg ) of A and B are respectively:
questions.solution:
Initially $\rightarrow$ 2 moles of + 3 moles of B
$X_A = \frac{2}{5}$ and $X_B = \frac{3}{5}$
$P_s = P_A^{\circ}X_A + P_B^{\circ}X_B$
$320 = P_A^{\circ}\left(\frac{2}{5}\right) + P_B^{\circ}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)$
$2P_A^{\circ} + 3P_B^{\circ} = 1600$
Now 1 mole of A and 1 mole of B is added
$X_A' = \frac{3}{7}$ and $X_B' = \frac{4}{7}$
$P_s' = P_A^{\circ}X_A' + P_B^{\circ}X_B'$
$328.57 = P_A^{\circ}\left(\frac{3}{7}\right) + P_B^{\circ}\left(\frac{4}{7}\right)$
$3P_A^{\circ} + 4P_B^{\circ} = 2300$
on solving these two equations
$P_A^{\circ} = 200$ mm of Hg
$P_B^{\circ} = 500$ mm of Hg

questions.stem:
$\mathrm{Ph{-}CH{=}CH_2} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{HBr}]{\mathrm{(PhCOO)_2}}$ Product
Consider the above reaction
A. The reaction proceeds through a more stable radical intermediate.
B. The role of peroxide is to generate $\mathrm{H^{\bullet}}$ (Hydrogen radical).
C. During this reaction, benzene is formed as a byproduct.
D. 1-Bromo-2-phenylethane is formed as the minor product.
E. The same reaction in absence of peroxide proceeds via carbocation intermediate.
Identify the correct statements. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{Ph{-}CH{=}CH_2} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{HBr/(PhCOO)_2}} \mathrm{Ph{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}Br}$ (anti M.K. addition)
Mechanism : $\mathrm{Ph{-}CO{-}O{-}O{-}CO{-}Ph} \xrightarrow[\text{(Homolysis)}]{\Delta} \mathrm{2Ph{-}CO{-}O^{\bullet}}$
$\mathrm{Ph{-}CO{-}O^{\bullet}} \xrightarrow{-\mathrm{CO_2}} \mathrm{Ph^{\bullet}}$; $\mathrm{Ph^{\bullet}} + \mathrm{H{-}Br} \rightarrow \mathrm{Ph{-}H} + \mathrm{Br^{\bullet}}$
$\mathrm{Ph{-}CH{=}CH_2} + \mathrm{Br^{\bullet}} \rightarrow \mathrm{Ph{-}\dot{C}H{-}CH_2Br}$ (Stable) $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{H{-}Br}} \mathrm{Ph{-}CH_2{-}CH_2Br} + \mathrm{Br^{\bullet}}$
A $\Rightarrow$ Correct
B $\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{Br^{\bullet}}$ is generated not $\mathrm{H^{\bullet}}$
C $\Rightarrow$ Correct
D $\Rightarrow$ This is major Product (incorrect)
E $\Rightarrow$ In absence of peroxide M.K. addition takes place. (Correct)

questions.stem:
$20.0\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ of an ideal gas ' X ' at 600 K and 0.5 MPa undergoes isothermal reversible expansion until pressure of the gas is 0.2 MPa . Which of the following option is correct?
(Given : $\log 2 = 0.3010$ and $\log 5 = 0.6989$)
questions.solution:
$P_1 = 0.5$ M Pa
$P_2 = 0.2$ M Pa
T = 600 K
For isothermal process $\Delta U = 0$ and $\Delta H = 0$
$\Delta U = q + W$
$\Delta U = 0$ (isothermal)
$q = -W$
$W = -nRT\ln\left(\frac{P_1}{P_2}\right)$
$W = -2.303nRT\log\left(\frac{P_1}{P_2}\right)$
(PV = nRT)
$W = -2.303\left(P_1V_1\right)\log\left(\frac{P_1}{P_2}\right)$
$W = -2.303 \times \left(0.5 \times 10^{6}\right) \times \left(20 \times 10^{-3}\right)\log\left(\frac{0.5}{0.2}\right)$
$W = -9.1$ kJ
$q = -W = 9.1$ kJ

[Given: Molar mass in $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ H : 1, C : 12, Br : 80, Ag : 108, O : 16 ; Compound(x) : $\mathrm{C_xH_yBr_z}$ ]
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{C_xH_yBr_z} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{AgNO_3}\ \text{Solution}]{\text{Conc.}\mathrm{HNO_3}} \mathrm{AgBr}\downarrow$
(O.C.) 0.53 gm | 0.75 gm
$\%\mathrm{Br} = \frac{80}{188} \times \frac{W_{\mathrm{AgBr}}}{W_{\mathrm{O.C.}}} \times 100$
$= \frac{80}{188} \times \frac{0.75}{0.53} \times 100 = 60.21\%$
$\mathrm{C_xH_yBr_z} \xrightarrow[\text{(Burn)}]{\mathrm{CuO}/\Delta} x\mathrm{CO_2}$
(O.C.) 1 gm | 1.32 gm
$\%\mathrm{C} = \frac{12}{44} \times \frac{W_{\mathrm{CO_2}}}{W_{\mathrm{O.C.}}} \times 100$
$= \frac{12}{44} \times \frac{1.32}{1} \times 100 = 36\%$
% H = 100 – (% of Br + % of C)
= 100 – (60.21 + 36) $\Rightarrow$ 100 – 96.21 = 3.79% $\simeq$ 4%

questions.stem:
Consider the dissociation equilibrium of the following weak acid
$\mathrm{HA \rightleftharpoons H^+(aq) + A^-(aq)}$
If the pKa of the acid is 4 , then the pH of 10 mM HA solution is ______.(Nearest integer)
[Given: The degree of dissociation can be neglected with respect to unity]
questions.solution:
[HA] = 10 mM = $10^{-2}$ M
$\mathrm{p}K_a = 4$, $K_a = 10^{-4}$
$\mathrm{HA \rightleftharpoons H^+ + A^-}$
$10^{-2}$
$10^{-2} - x$ | $x$ | $x$   $\left[\alpha = \frac{x}{10^{-2}}\right]$
$10^{-2} - 10^{-2}\alpha$ | $10^{-2}\alpha$ | $10^{-2}\alpha$   $x = 10^{-2}\alpha$
$K_a = \frac{\left(10^{-2}\alpha\right)\left(10^{-2}\alpha\right)}{10^{-2}\left(1 - \alpha\right)}$   $\left(\alpha \ll 1,\ 1 - \alpha \approx 1\right)$
$10^{-4} = 10^{-2}\alpha^{2}$
$\alpha = 10^{-1}$
$[\mathrm{H^+}] = 10^{-2}\alpha = 10^{-3}$
$\mathrm{pH} = -\log[\mathrm{H^+}]$
= 3

questions.stem: 500 mL of 1.2 M KI solution is mixed with 500 mL of 0.2 M $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ solution in basic medium. The liberated iodine was titrated with standard 0.1 M $\mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3}$ solution in the presence of starch indicator till the blue color disappeared. The volume (in L ) of $\mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3}$ consumed is _____. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{KI + KMnO_4 \xrightarrow{OH^-} MnO_2 + I_2}$
KI: n-factor = 1; $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$: n-factor = 3
Milli equivalents of KI = $1.2 \times 500 \times 1 = 600$
Milli equivalents of $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ = $0.2 \times 500 \times 3 = 300$
Milli equivalents of $\mathrm{I_2}$ formed = 300
$\mathrm{I_2 + Na_2S_2O_3 \rightarrow NaI + Na_2S_4O_6}$
Milli equivalents of $\mathrm{I_2}$ = Milli equivalents of $\mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3}$
$300 = M \times V(\mathrm{ml}) \times$ n-factor
$300 = 0.1 \times V(\mathrm{ml}) \times 1$
V = 3000 ml
V = 3L
